questions.prompt: Order the effort levels from lowest to highest.
questions.explanation: The five levels run Low, Medium, High, Extra high (xhigh), and Max.

questions.prompt: Which effort level does the Help Center describe as the best overall balance of quality and speed?
questions.explanation: Low and Medium suit routine tasks, High is the best overall balance, Extra high targets long-running coding and agentic tasks, and Max is the most thorough.

questions.prompt: On the newest models, thinking can't be turned off in the apps, so ____ is your main control over how much work Claude does.
questions.explanation: Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, and Opus 5 always think in the apps; effort sets how much.

questions.prompt: Match each task to a sensible starting setup.

pairs.right: Haiku or Sonnet at Low/Medium effort

pairs.left: The hardest reasoning problem you have
pairs.right: Fable at High or Max effort

questions.explanation: Match the dials to the task: light settings for simple work, stronger models and more effort for complex and long-running work.

questions.prompt: Which are true about higher effort? Select all that apply.

options.text: It uses more tokens and more of your limit
It fixes prompts that are missing context

questions.explanation: Higher effort is more thorough but slower and uses more tokens. It doesn't supply context your prompt left out, so fix the prompt first.

questions.prompt: An answer looks wrong on a hard problem. What should you check first?

options.text: Your prompt: is important context missing?

questions.explanation: Missing context or vague instructions are often the real cause. Fix the prompt, then raise effort or switch models, and read the thinking summary for faulty assumptions.
